options.text: Lake Toba (in North Sumatra is) the largest lake in Indonesia.
options.why: Is belongs to the main sentence, so it should be outside the brackets.

options.text: Lake Toba (in North Sumatra) is the largest lake in Indonesia.
(Lake Toba) in North Sumatra is the largest lake in Indonesia.
options.why: Lake Toba is the subject of the sentence, so it should not be in brackets.

options.text: Lake Toba in (North Sumatra is the largest lake) in Indonesia.
options.why: The brackets hold part of the main sentence.

hints: Brackets hold extra information.
Read each sentence without the words in brackets. It should still make sense.
Which words tell you extra information about where Lake Toba is?
items.explanation: In North Sumatra is extra information, so it goes in brackets. Lake Toba is the largest lake in Indonesia makes sense without it.

options.text: a small girl
options.why: Small describes the girl on its own, so no hyphen is needed.

options.text: a ten year old girl
a happy girl
options.why: Happy describes the girl on its own.

options.text: a girl who is ten
options.why: Ten comes after the noun here, so no hyphens are needed.

hints: Hyphens join words that work together to describe a noun.
Look for a group of words before the noun that act as one describing word.
Ask: do ten, year and old describe the girl together?
items.explanation: Ten, year and old work together to describe the girl, so they are joined with hyphens: a ten-year-old girl.

items.prompt: Two words should be joined with a hyphen. Write them with the hyphen. My sister is a well known singer.
hints: Look at the words just before singer.
Two words that describe a noun together are often joined with a hyphen.
Find the two words that tell us what kind of singer she is.
items.explanation: Well and known work together to describe singer, so they are joined: a well-known singer.

items.prompt: Which punctuation could replace the brackets? Our teacher (Mr Halim) loves astronomy.

options.text: a pair of commas
a pair of full stops
options.why: Full stops would break the sentence into pieces.

options.text: a pair of colons
options.why: Colons introduce lists or explanations.

options.text: a pair of question marks
options.why: Question marks end questions.

hints: Brackets mark extra information.
Another pair of punctuation marks can also mark extra information.
Try reading the sentence with a short pause before and after Mr Halim.
items.explanation: A pair of commas can also mark extra information: Our teacher, Mr Halim, loves astronomy.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly to add extra information?

options.text: Pak Joko the school, gardener grows orchids.
options.why: The commas should go around the school gardener.

options.text: Pak Joko, the school gardener grows orchids.
options.why: The extra information needs a comma at the end too.

options.text: Pak Joko, the school gardener, grows orchids.
Pak, Joko the school gardener, grows orchids.
options.why: The first comma should come after Joko, not after Pak.

hints: Find the extra information about Pak Joko.
Extra information needs a comma before it and a comma after it.
Read the sentence without the school gardener. Does it still make sense?
items.explanation: The school gardener is extra information about Pak Joko, so it has a comma on each side.

items.prompt: Which sentence means that the chair will be given a new cover?

options.text: We will recover the old chair.
options.why: Recover means get something back or get better after an illness.

options.text: We will discover the old chair.
options.why: Discover means find.

options.text: We will uncover the old chair.
options.why: Uncover means take a cover off.

options.text: We will re-cover the old chair.

hints: The hyphen changes how the word is read.
Re- means again, so re-cover means cover again.
Replace the long word in each sentence with its meaning. Which one is about a new cover?
items.explanation: Re-cover with a hyphen means cover again. Without the hyphen, recover means get better or get something back.

items.prompt: Sort the phrases: does it need a hyphen or not?
hints: Hyphens join words that work together as one describing word or one name.
If the describing words come before the noun, they often need a hyphen.
Start with a fast moving river. Do fast and moving work together to describe the river?
items.explanation: A fast-moving river, a sugar-free drink and my mother-in-law need hyphens. In the other phrases, the words come after the noun or work separately.

items.prompt: Add brackets. Write the words that should go inside them. The Komodo dragon the largest lizard in the world can be found in Indonesia.

answers: the largest lizard in the world

hints: Brackets hold extra information that the sentence could manage without.
Find the words that describe the Komodo dragon.
Read the sentence without those words. Does it still make sense?
items.explanation: The largest lizard in the world is extra information about the Komodo dragon, so it goes in brackets.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences that are punctuated correctly.

options.text: The concert (which started late) was wonderful.
My brother, a keen cyclist, rode 40 kilometres.
The film (was) very exciting.
options.why: Was belongs to the main sentence and should not be in brackets.

options.text: We saw a twelve-metre-long whale shark.
A sugar, free drink is healthier.
options.why: Sugar-free needs a hyphen, not a comma.

hints: Check each pair of brackets, each pair of commas and each hyphen.
Extra information must be removable. Hyphens join words that describe a noun together.
Read each sentence without the bracketed or comma-marked words. Does it still work?
items.explanation: The correct sentences mark extra information with brackets or a pair of commas, and twelve-metre-long uses hyphens to describe the whale shark.

items.prompt: Which sentence means that about thirty people came to the party?

options.text: Thirty-odd people came to the party.
Thirty odd people came to the party.
options.why: Without a hyphen, odd describes the people, so it means thirty strange people!

options.text: Thirty, odd people came to the party.
options.why: The comma makes this confusing and does not mean about thirty.

options.text: Thirty (odd) people came to the party.
options.why: The brackets make odd extra information about the people.

hints: Odd can mean strange, but it can also mean roughly or a few more than.
A hyphen joins a number to odd when it means roughly that number.
Look for the sentence where thirty and odd are joined.
items.explanation: Thirty-odd means about thirty. Without the hyphen, thirty odd people means thirty strange people.
